sources.title: OECD Economic Surveys: Romania 2026, Enhancing resilience to climate risks
sources.organization: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
sources.temporal_coverage: National heat-stress data through 2024; disaster records 1980–2023; flood-plan implementation status and adaptation discussion in the 2026 survey.
sources.methodology: OECD survey synthesizes climate indicators, national records and cited sectoral studies.
sources.limitations: Loss and exposure estimates are national or basin-scale; the report does not evaluate each local project.

sources.title: Assessment of progress on climate adaptation in the individual Member States according to the European Climate Law
sources.temporal_coverage: Assessment of Romania's adaptation reports for 2021 and 2023; covers reported projections, institutions and municipal initiatives.
sources.methodology: Commission assessed Romania's 2021 and 2023 EU Climate Law adaptation submissions.
sources.limitations: Implementation and impact detail are often unavailable.

sources.title: UCPM Peer Review Report: Romania 2023
sources.organization: European Commission, Union Civil Protection Mechanism Peer Review Programme
sources.temporal_coverage: Disaster-risk-management peer review conducted in 2023; country-profile annex includes indicators based on 2015–2022 data and mid-century scenarios.
sources.methodology: EU civil-protection peer review drew on Romanian authorities and stakeholder consultations and includes a country-profile annex.
sources.limitations: The annex compiles external risk indices; its conflict projection does not identify a mechanism or model details.

sources.title: România și-ar putea îmbunătăți substanțial nivelul de trai concomitent cu decarbonizarea economiei până în 2050: raportul Grupului Banca Mondială
sources.temporal_coverage: World Bank summary of its October 2023 Romania Country Climate and Development Report and selected recommendations.
sources.methodology: World Bank press release summarizes findings and recommendations from its 2023 Romania CCDR.
sources.limitations: Press release is a summary; the detailed report PDF was not accessible.

sources.title: Romania, EU Mission on Adaptation to Climate Change portal
sources.organization: European Commission, Directorate-General for Climate Action
sources.temporal_coverage: Portal counts and funding displayed in June 2026; localized mountain-meadow adaptation example in Râu Sadului and Cristian.
sources.methodology: EU Mission portal lists Romanian adaptation participants, funding and example projects.
sources.limitations: Portal stories are selected examples, not impact evaluations.

claims.locator: Section 3.1.2, Romania is particularly exposed to droughts, heatwaves and river flooding
claims.paraphrase: During 2020–2024 Romania averaged 18 additional heat-stress days versus 1981–2010, reaching 48 annually and about 13 tropical nights.
claims.limitations: National aggregate; observation period ends in 2024.

claims.locator: Section 3.1.2, Romania is particularly exposed to droughts, heatwaves and river flooding
claims.paraphrase: In Romania's Danube Basin, about 25% of the population and 8% of territory are flood-exposed; Danube and Siret floods peak in spring and early summer.
claims.limitations: Risk estimates are not counts of affected people.

claims.locator: Section 3.1.2, Romania is particularly exposed to droughts, heatwaves and river flooding
claims.paraphrase: OECD reports droughts in 2020, 2022 and 2024 harmed agricultural output, agrifood prices and hydropower generation.

claims.locator: Section 3.2.2, Better managing land-use planning and urban development in flood-prone areas
claims.paraphrase: OECD describes urban expansion in Constanța County coastal towns without sufficient elevation or drainage upgrades despite known pluvial and coastal flood risks.
claims.limitations: The survey gives no town-specific exposure count.

claims.locator: Section 3.2.2, Speeding up the implementation of flood protection measures
claims.paraphrase: Of 2,627 second-cycle flood-plan actions (2016–2021), 67% had not started; local authorities lacked finance and expertise, while Romanian Waters lacked scale-up capacity.
claims.limitations: Plan cycles are historical; implementation status is as reported by OECD in 2026.

claims.locator: Romania country assessment, Section 1, changes to reported vulnerabilities and risks since 2021
claims.paraphrase: The Commission says drought is the key agricultural hazard and crop-failure risk is greatest in southern and southeastern Romania; PESETA IV estimates losses 16% higher at +2°C.
claims.scenario: PESETA IV estimate for a world 2.0°C warmer than present; projected agricultural losses by value.
claims.limitations: Modelled relative to present, not an observed loss.

claims.locator: Romania country assessment, Section 1, climate monitoring and modelling framework
claims.paraphrase: Romania reported 166 weather stations, including 68 agrometeorological stations, and seven Doppler radars; 2023 regional modelling aimed at high-resolution subregional projections.
claims.limitations: The Commission noted computing constraints and limited collaboration with model users.

claims.locator: Romania country assessment, Sections 2 and 4, institutional coordination and monitoring
claims.paraphrase: The Commission identified weak coordination between climate-adaptation and disaster-risk authorities, limited finance and no demonstrated national monitoring of adaptation goals.
institutions: Ministry of Environment, Water and Forests
claims.limitations: Assessment reflects 2023 reporting and not subsequent institutional reforms.

claims.locator: Romania country assessment, Section 6, subnational policies and cooperation
claims.paraphrase: Romania cited Alba Iulia's municipal plan as good practice and reported two regions joining the EU Adaptation Mission.

claims.locator: Romania country assessment, Section 5, cooperation and transnational projects
claims.paraphrase: A Danube-macroregion project linked shared risk-assessment methods and drought-emergency response among 14 partners from nine countries.
geographies: Romania and eight other participating countries

claims.locator: Annex 3, Romania Country Profile, climate-change analysis paragraph on humanitarian and conflict risk
claims.paraphrase: The profile's climate-change analysis projects by mid-century 3–5.2 million additional people exposed to drought and 2.6–4.4 million to vector-borne epidemics; it says conflict risk may rise except under SSP5.
claims.scenario: Mid-century humanitarian-risk projections include RCP4.5–SSP1 and RCP8.5–SSP3; the annex says conflict risk may rise in all scenarios except SSP5.
affected_groups: additional people exposed under modeled scenarios
institutions: Union Civil Protection Mechanism Peer Review Programme
claims.limitations: The profile gives no conflict model, causal pathway, mediator or uncertainty bounds.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The profile's climate-change analysis says conflict risk may increase except under SSP5, but specifies no mechanism.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Annex 3, Romania Country Profile, climate-change analysis paragraph on humanitarian and conflict risk

claims.locator: Annex 3, Romania Country Profile, adaptive capacity discussion
claims.paraphrase: The profile places eastern Romania at lower adaptive capacity than central and western regions, citing weaker institutional capacity and knowledge/technology factors.
claims.limitations: Index comparison uses 2022-era inputs; regions are not individually named.

claims.locator: Section 3.1, National Risk Assessment and the RO-RISK project; Section 3.4, Monitoring, evaluation and reporting
claims.paraphrase: Reviewers reported risk assessment was irregular after RO-RISK ended in 2018; risk and disaster-loss data were scattered across national, county and local entities and inconsistent.
claims.limitations: Peer-review findings date to 2023; no later status update was inspected.

claims.locator: Paragraph beginning România este deosebit de vulnerabilă la riscurile asociate schimbărilor climatice
claims.paraphrase: World Bank describes Romania as particularly vulnerable to climate-related floods and drought; rising temperatures and heatwaves threaten people, the economy and infrastructure.
claims.limitations: Press-release summary provides no subnational breakdown.

claims.locator: Paragraph beginning Optimizarea utilizării resurselor de apă
claims.paraphrase: CCDR calls water deficits a current concern and priority for strategic management, with implications for power generation, agriculture and consumers.
claims.limitations: Press-release summary specifies no locality or water-deficit measure.

claims.locator: Paragraph beginning Investiția în capitalul uman și competențe
claims.paraphrase: CCDR recommends skills development and active labour-market policies to help vulnerable groups adapt to Romania's green-economy transition.
claims.limitations: These are proposed policies, not evaluated delivery or impact.

claims.locator: The Mission in Romania, participation and funding paragraph dated 26 June 2026
claims.paraphrase: As of June 2026, 25 Romanian local/regional authorities participated in Mission projects, with nine Charter signatories and €11.66 million EU funding allocated.
institutions: EU Mission on Adaptation to Climate Change
claims.limitations: Participation and allocated funding do not establish outcomes.

claims.locator: Real-world adaptation example, mountain-meadow story for Râu Sadului and Cristian
claims.paraphrase: In Râu Sadului and Cristian mountain communities, projects restore 40 hectares of degraded meadows to address drought, biodiversity loss and soil erosion, using drones for field operations.
institutions: EU Mission on Adaptation to Climate Change
claims.limitations: Portal presents a short case summary, not measured resilience outcomes.

search_audit.query: Romania climate vulnerability drought flood Danube Siret counties local adaptation report
search_audit.outcome: Direct OECD, Commission, and EU Mission texts supplied basin, county, subregional and named-community findings. Indexed hits on the inaccessible 2026 Commission report and ICPDR page were not used.

search_audit.query: Romania climate change conflict violence fragility climate security report resource conflict primary source
search_audit.outcome: The 2023 UCPM country-profile annex directly states a mid-century conflict-risk projection within its climate-change analysis, but specifies no conflict mediator or mechanism. No other directly read source-stated pathway was found.

search_audit.query: Romania Ukraine refugee displaced conflict climate adaptation local government capacity report climate resilience
search_audit.outcome: Search results included reports on Ukrainian displacement and integration, but no directly read primary source linked conflict or displacement to climate-adaptation constraints in Romania. Search-result text was not used as evidence.

search_audit.query: Romania climate adaptation local capacity implementation municipal county community report
search_audit.outcome: Direct reports describe flood-plan implementation gaps and local-government capacity limits, while the Commission and Mission portal report municipal planning, cross-border drought coordination, and named meadow restoration. These are adaptation and disaster-risk capacities, not additional FCV evidence.

gaps: No directly read primary source established an FCV-to-climate-adaptation mechanism for Romania; search results on displacement were leads only.
The UCPM profile's climate-scenario statement that conflict risk may rise provides no conflict mechanism, model details or uncertainty bounds; it is retained only as that source-stated projection.
The linked full Romania CCDR and the 2026 European Commission country-report PDF could not be directly accessed; their indexed text was excluded.
The ICPDR Danube Delta publisher page returned 403; its indexed summary was excluded from evidence.
